title: Preview Fabric Information
content: ### Objective Preview Fabric information in the Library window. ### Location Library ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric File (.zfab) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Library ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric File (.zfab) → Preview of Fabric files is now being displayed below the Library section. ※ Note: Only fabric files saved in Marvelous Designer 4 and above are allowed to display Fabric information preview. For any fabric files created in previous versions, need to be saved again in ver3.1.0 or above (ver3.1.0).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to preview fabric information from .zfab files in the Library window of Marvelous Designer, ensuring compatibility with version 4 and above.

title: ZIPPER: Slider Gizmo
content: ### Objective Move or rotate the slider to adjust its distance from the zipper tape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Move 1. Create a zipper. 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its Gizmo appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. #### Rotate 1. With the Select/Move tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. ※ Note: To reset the slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select the Reset Slider Arrangement option.
content_description: This webpage guides users on how to adjust the position and orientation of a zipper slider within a 3D garment simulation.

title: Add Color Swatch
content: ### Objective Add color swatches to custom palette. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color ▶ Color Palette Window ▶ Add ### Operation 1. Select a desired object; Avatar/Fabric/Button/Topstitch/Etc. 2. Click on Color in the Property Editor. → The Color Palette window appears. 3. Select a desired color from Open Palette or Palette Library. 4. Follow the indicated guideline below: Color Palette Window ▶ Add → The selected color is now being added to the custom palette.
content_description: "Learn how to easily add color swatches to your custom palette using the Color Palette window in the Property Editor."

title: Create Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole ### Operation #### Create Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. → A buttonhole is created. 3. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. → The buttonholes are now being created. #### Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Buttonhole 3D Toolbar ▶ Buttonhole 2. Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. → The Moving Distance window appears. 3. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. → Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click OK to place. → The buttonholes are now being created.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to create and accurately position buttonholes on a 3D garment or 2D pattern using intuitive tools and measurements.

title: Tack
content: ### Objective Use this function to visualize fit adjustments by tacking temporarily. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack 2. Click on an initial point on a draped Garment. → A point is now being created with a dotted line following. 3. Click on an endpoint. → Another point is now being created with a yellow highlighted line. → Same tack is now being created in the 2D Pattern. 4. Activate Simulate. → The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to each other. ※ Note: It is also available to create and modify tacks in the 2D window (ver3.1.0). ###
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for visualizing fit adjustments in garment design using the Tack function in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Piping Property Setting
content: ### Objective Modify the physical Piping properties at Property Editor. ### Location Property Editor ### Explanation Piping properties appear in the Property Editor when a Piping is selected with the Select/Move tool or the Edit Piping tool. Information | Name | Renames selected Piping. ---|---|--- Line Length | Displays the line length of selected Piping. Dimension | Width (mm) | Adjusts the width of selected Piping between the value of 1~15mm. Particle Distance (mm) | Adjusts the Particle Distance of selected Piping between the value of 1~5mm. Finishing | Start | Close start of piping End | Close end of piping | Fabric | Applies fabric settings to selected Piping from the drop-down item list of Fabric. Piping's fabric texture can be edited using the edit_texture.png Edit Texture tool (ver4.2.0). Hide | Shows/hides selected Piping. (Select a Piping from the Scene tab in the Object Browser to reveal menu.)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to modifying the physical properties of piping through the Property Editor, including adjustments for dimensions, particle distance, fabric settings, and visibility options.

title: Play Motion
content: ### Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion ### Operation #### Pose 1. Open a Pose file. → When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Play Motion 2D Toolbar ▶ Play Motion 3. Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. → The Avatar stops temporarily. → The Avatar changes pose again. #### Motion 1. Open a Motion file. → The Play Motion tool now can be selected. 2. Click the Play Motion tool. → The motion is played. * The Transition Animation for the default avatars of the version 10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for using the Play Motion tool to animate avatars by loading Pose or Motion files.

title: Edit Texture Size (Property Editor)

Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric (Select the Desired One) ▶ Property Editor → The selected Fabric's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the Transformation option which only appears when a texture is applied to a Pattern. Option | Description ---|--- Angle | Type in the rotating angle. Width | Set the texture width. Height | Set the texture height. Lock Aspect Ratio | Lock the width and height ratio.

title: Reset Topstitch Style Property

title: 3D M:N Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: The M:N Free Sewing web page empowers users to effortlessly create and manage Sewing Lines across multiple patterns in both 2D and 3D environments, facilitating efficient and precise pattern assembly.

When setting the Topstitch on the Pattern's cutting line, the Topstitches always appear on the inside of a Garment and the Flip function gets deactivated. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶Flip ### Operation 1. Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶Flip → The Topstitch direction will now be changed.

title: Add Bounding Voulme
content: ### Objective Add a Bounding Volume to add arrangement points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Add ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Add → A new Bounding Volume called "Pan" is now being created at the bottom of the Bounding Volume list, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2\. Set details for Bounding Volume. Board | Check the list of currently added layouts and edit the properties of the layout by selecting the desired item. ---|--- Name | Changes the name of the Bounding Volume. Arrangement BV | Joint Name 0 | Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume starts. Joint Name 1 | Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume ends. Shape (ver MD10) | Depending on the shape of the Avatar, the Bounding Volume is set to the Cylinder and Cuboid. Height | Sets the height of the Bounding Volume. Length X | Adjusts the circumference of the left and right radii of the Bounding Volume. Length Y | Adjusts the circumference of the top and bottom radii of the Bounding Volume. Round Corner (ver MD10) | ※ It is active only when the Bounding Volume type is set to Cuboid. Adjust the radius of each corner. Hands/Feet | If this option is activated, the length of the Bounding Volume is adjusted to the avatar's hands and feet. The moment you click that option, the entire Bounding Volume is refreshed. ※ Note: If the order below/above the joint points is reversed, the left and right sides are flipped when arranging the Pattern.
content_description: This web page guides users through the process of adding and configuring a Bounding Volume for arrangement points within the Avatar Editor.

title: I got an email titled "Update Required: Your account is on hold." What does it mean?
content: # **New License Status Policy Announcement: License Suspension After Payment Failure** **Q. I got an email titled "Update Required: Your account is on hold." What does it mean?** **A:** You received this email because your payment attempt during the checkout process failed. This can happen due to reasons such as: * Insufficient funds * Expired credit card * Declined transaction As a result, your license was not activated, and the system has automatically suspended your license status until a successful payment is completed. ⏳ A 7-day grace period is provided, during which the system will attempt two automatic retries to process the payment. * The first retry will occur 3 days later, and the second retry will take place on the final day of the suspension period. If either payments fails, your subscription will be automatically canceled. * * * ## ## **How to Reactivate Your License** 1. Go to “[ _**My Account > License**_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/license)” and update your payment method if you wish to continue your subscription. 2. If at least one of the two retry attempts succeeds, the subscription will be reinstated. 3. If you wish to cancel your subscription, a Cancel button is available in the “[ _**My Account > License**_](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/license) _**”**_ section. ## **Additional Notes** Only personal monthly licenses (recurring payment including trial license) are eligible for suspension and reactivation. This policy does not apply to: * Personal 1 Year Licenses * Enterprise Licenses * Student Licenses
content_description: Stay informed about our new license status policy, which includes automatic suspension after payment failure and essential steps to reactivate your subscription.

title: Automatically Create Fitting Suit at Import
content: ### Objective Automatically generate a Fitting Suit for a custom bipedal avatar at import. * * * ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ/FBX ▶ **Auto Create Fitting Suit**. **** ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". 2. Select either OBJ or FBX file format for import. 3. Navigate to the file location for a custom bipedal avatar (two arms, two legs, no tail) in either A-Pose or T-Pose, and double-click on the file name. → The Import OBJ/FBX pop-up Window appears. 4. Make sure the **Load Type** is set to **Open** and the **Object Type** is set to **Avatar**. 5. Check the option box next to **Auto Create Fitting Suit** 6. Click on **OK**. → The Avatar is imported into the scene and a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the process.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for automatically generating a fitting suit for custom bipedal avatars during the import process of OBJ or FBX files.

title: Marvelous Designer Standalone License Transition
content: **Effective Date:** December 2, 2025 This document outlines the discontinuation of the Marvelous Designer Standalone license and establishes the transition procedures for all existing Standalone license holders. As of the Effective Date, the Marvelous Designer Standalone Online license will be retired and will no longer be available for purchase. ## **Continued Support for Existing Licenses** All existing Standalone licenses will continue to be fully supported and will retain all current features until their expiration date. #### ## **Transition Offer for Annual Standalone Licenses** To facilitate a seamless transition, a transition offer is being provided for a grace period to all Annual Standalone license holders. * **Offer Period:** The grace period for this offer is from the Effective Date until **June 30, 2026**. * **Transition Option:** During this period, users can transition to a Network Online license at the same annual renewal price of **$1900 USD per license**. * **Automatic Upgrade:** Upon renewal, the user’s existing Annual Standalone license will be automatically upgraded to a Network Online License for the remainder of its current term, in addition to the new annual term. #### ## **Transition for Monthly Standalone Licenses** * All existing Monthly Standalone license holders will be seamlessly transitioned to the new Subscription License * This license shall provide the same feature to that of the current Monthly Standalone License without the node-lock system. #### ## **Table of Enterprise Licenses as of Dec. 2** **Name** | **Price** | **Description** | **OS** ---|---|---|--- ENTERPRISE MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION | $199/month | Full MD experience with limited Userpool feature Only available via subscription on the website | Windows, Mac ENTERPRISE ANNUAL NETWORK | $2,000/year | Full MD experience with Userpool feature | Windows, Mac ENTERPRISE LINUX | $2,300/year | Full MD experience with Userpool feature | Linux only *The Userpool feature simplifies user account management, allowing you to easily assign purchased licenses to multiple end-user IDs. ([Userpool Manual](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358149827609-User-Pool-Manual))
content_description: This webpage serves to inform existing Marvelous Designer Standalone license holders about the upcoming discontinuation of their licenses and the transition options available to ensure continued access to features and support.
